item.description: [BJJ] ADCC loses Fornarino (4th defending champ) to UFC BJJ 10 Grand Prix; Michell removed. UFC BJJ 10 Women's Flyweight Grand Prix announced Aug 20. PSS 7 tonight in Miami. [Soccer] Arsenal & Atletico agree framework on Gyokeres-Alvarez swap. Man Utd lost pre-season opener. [Finance] Tesla -14.5%, S&P -1.21% on earnings miss; AAPL at $321, 6 days to earnings. [NJ] Free Infernos concert tonight at Brookdale Park; Newark Museum clay workshop closes Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu & Submission Grappling

  • ADCC Krakow Loses 4th Defending Champion — Fornarino Exits for UFC BJJ 10 Grand Prix; Michell Removed
    Reigning ADCC -55kg double gold medalist Adele Fornarino has been pulled from the Krakow 2026 roster after choosing to compete in the inaugural Women's Flyweight Grand Prix at UFC BJJ 10 (August 20), while ADCC Asia & Oceania Trials winner Izaak Michell was simultaneously removed over an active Texas arrest warrant — the 4th and 5th departures from a September 12-13 bracket that has now lost five confirmed competitors in quick succession.
    Source: MMA Mania
  • UFC BJJ 10 Announces Inaugural Women's Flyweight Grand Prix for August 20 — Fornarino vs. Brunacio Headline
    The UFC's no-gi grappling series announced a landmark addition to its August 20 card at the Meta Apex: the first-ever Women's Flyweight Grand Prix at UFC BJJ 10, with ADCC double champion Adele Fornarino facing Brazilian standout Carol Brunacio in the tournament semifinals — the winner of the four-woman bracket will be crowned the inaugural UFC BJJ Women's Flyweight Champion.
    Source: Jits Magazine
  • PSS 7 Tonight in Miami: Jacob Rodriguez vs. Vagner Rocha Live at Karate Combat 62 — ADCC 7 Weeks Out
    Tonight's Karate Combat 62 / Pit Submission Series 7 card in Miami features Jacob Rodriguez ending a 17-month competitive absence against veteran Vagner Rocha in the PSS main event — a high-stakes grappling match just seven weeks before ADCC Krakow, with both men expected to compete at the September 12-13 World Championship.
    Source: Yahoo Sports

Global & European Soccer

  • Reports: Arsenal and Atletico Reach Framework Agreement on Gyokeres-Alvarez Swap — Alvarez's Approval the Last Hurdle
    Football365 reports Arsenal and Atletico Madrid have agreed on a deal structure — Viktor Gyokeres plus €50M cash for Julian Alvarez — but the transfer remains stalled as Alvarez still prefers a move to Barcelona, a destination Atletico refuses to facilitate regardless of the fee on offer.
    Source: Football365
  • Man United Stumble 1-0 to Wrexham in Pre-Season Opener Ahead of August 1 Atletico Stockholm Test
    Manchester United began their 2026-27 pre-season with a 1-0 defeat to Championship club Wrexham in Helsinki, then face Rosenborg in Trondheim before traveling to Stockholm for the August 1 friendly against La Liga champions Atletico Madrid — a match that will serve as the first meaningful test for both clubs' summer signings.
    Source: Sports Mole
  • Atletico's New Trio Ready for Stockholm — Grimaldo, Hjulmand, and Kang-in Set for First Pre-Season Test
    With world cup finalists returning to Majadahonda by July 28, Atletico Madrid's three summer signings — left-back Alejandro Grimaldo, holding midfielder Morten Hjulmand, and creative South Korean midfielder Lee Kang-in — will finally train with the full squad ahead of the August 1 Stockholm friendly, giving Simeone his first real look at the new-look La Liga champions in a competitive setting.
    Source: Atletico Madrid Official

Financial Freedom & Markets

  • Tesla Tanks 14.5% on Q2 Earnings Miss — S&P 500 Sinks 1.21%, Nasdaq Falls 2.15%, VTI Under Pressure
    Tesla's Q2 report (July 23) beat on revenue ($28.2B, +26% YoY) but badly missed on profits — EPS $0.33 vs. $0.51 expected, operating margin collapsing to just 1.4% — sending TSLA down roughly 14.5% and dragging the S&P 500 -1.21% to 7,408 and Nasdaq -2.15% to 25,137; VTI came under pressure as the Mag 7 rotation continues, with Apple's July 30 print now the market's single most critical near-term catalyst.
    Source: Teslarati
  • AAPL at $321.66 With 6 Days to Earnings — Citi Lifts Target to $365, Tim Cook's Final Call as CEO Approaches
    Apple shares are consolidating at $321.66 (down 0.56% Thursday) with just six days until the July 30 Q3 earnings call where EPS consensus stands at $1.88 on ~$109B revenue; Citi analyst Asiya Merchant raised her price target to $365 on July 13 on margin optimism, and in a significant milestone, July 30 will mark Tim Cook's final earnings call before John Ternus takes over as Apple CEO.
    Source: CNBC
  • SPOT +2.97% Outperforms Falling Market — 11 Days to August 4 Earnings; NJ Refinance Rates Ease to 6.70%
    Spotify shares gained 2.97% despite broad market weakness (11 days to August 4 Q2 earnings), with investor optimism building around cost discipline and operating income growth ahead of the report; separately, New Jersey's 30-year fixed refinance rate eased to 6.698% from its recent 7.02% peak — a modest relief for homeowners who've been waiting for a better entry window.
    Source: Yahoo Finance

NJ Local News (Montclair)

  • Free Outdoor Concert Tonight at Brookdale Park — The Infernos Headline Essex County Summer Music Series
    Tonight (Friday July 24) the Essex County free summer music series presents The Infernos at Brookdale Park on the Bloomfield/Montclair border — a no-cost outdoor show perfect for families heading into the Montclair Theater Festival weekend, and part of a recurring county series running throughout July and August.
    Source: Montclair Local
  • Newark Museum of Art Family Days Close Sunday July 26 — ‘Stars Are Everywhere’ Clay Seastars Workshop This Weekend
    The Newark Museum of Art's summer Family Fun Days run through this Sunday July 26 with a ‘Stars are everywhere’ theme — families can make textured Seastars from air-dry clay in hands-on workshops ideal for kids; it's a 30-minute drive from Montclair and a great complement to weekend theater festival or beach plans before the program wraps.
    Source: NJ Weekend Guide
  • Storytime With a Twist at Bloomfield Library — Balloon Animal Crafts for Kids Tomorrow, July 25 at 11am
    Bloomfield Public Library (minutes from Montclair) hosts Storytime with a Twist this Saturday July 25 at 11am, where children and caregivers read books together and then make their own balloon animals — a free, hands-on Saturday morning outing perfect for families looking for a calm alternative to the busy theater festival across town.
    Source: Patch

Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu & Submission Grappling

  • Mica Galvao Reinstated to ADCC Krakow 77kg Roster — Reversal Reshapes Most Contested Division
    FloGrappling's latest Grappling Bulletin confirms Mica Galvao has returned to the ADCC 2026 Krakow roster following his earlier withdrawal, a significant reversal that reshapes the stacked 77kg bracket at the September 12-13 World Championship and gives the division its full complement of elite contenders.
    Source: FloGrappling
  • 17-Year-Old Matilda Reid Wins ADCC Asia & Oceania +65kg in Gold Coast — 8 Athletes Qualify for Krakow
    Blue belt Matilda Reid, 17, dominated the +65kg bracket at the ADCC Asia & Oceania Trials in Gold Coast, Australia, defeating four more experienced opponents to claim the division title in what FloGrappling called the trials' standout result; all eight division champions — including Kaya Rudolph (-77kg, New Zealand) and Bekzat Kapashov (-66kg, Kazakhstan) — have punched their tickets to the September 12-13 World Championship.
    Source: FloGrappling
  • UFC BJJ 2 Co-Main Preview: Fowler vs. Garmo to Crown the First-Ever Light Heavyweight Champion
    With eight days until UFC BJJ 2 (July 31, free on YouTube at 8pm ET), the Fowler-Garmo co-main event is shaping up as the bout to watch — Mason Fowler brings a three-fight UFC BJJ submission run against a surging David Garmo, and the inaugural light heavyweight title gives the matchup lasting significance beyond a single night.
    Source: UFC

Global & European Soccer

  • Koke Renews Contract With Atletico Madrid Until June 2027 — One-Club Captain Commits for La Liga Title Defense
    Club captain Jorge Resurrección 'Koke' has signed a one-year contract extension keeping him at Atletico Madrid through June 2027, the club announced, with both parties activating an automatic renewal clause; the 34-year-old one-club man becomes the squad's continuity anchor in a summer that has seen significant turnover around him.
    Source: Yahoo Sports
  • Lee Kang-in Joins Atletico's Pre-Season Training — First Asian Player in Club History Begins Work Under Simeone
    South Korean midfielder Lee Kang-in — officially signed from PSG for approximately €35-40M in early July as Atletico's third summer arrival after Grimaldo and Hjulmand — is now integrating with the first-team squad in Majadahonda, giving Simeone a creative, high-energy option in midfield and making Kang-in the first Asian player in Atletico's history.
    Source: Into the Calderon
  • Atletico's 2026-27 Summer Scorecard: Three In, One Out, Salah Still Pursued Before La Liga Opener
    As Atletico's pre-season ramps up toward the August 1 Stockholm friendly vs. Manchester United, the summer transfer picture is mostly set: Grimaldo, Hjulmand, and Kang-in are confirmed signings; Alexander Sorloth's Juventus exit is imminent; Julian Alvarez stays; and Mohamed Salah's free agency remains the one outstanding question Simeone hopes to resolve before the late-August La Liga opener.
    Source: ESPN

Financial Freedom & Markets

  • Alphabet Q2 Beats on Revenue and Cloud — But GOOGL Sinks ~5% After Hours on Record $200B Capex Guidance
    Google parent Alphabet reported Q2 revenue of $119.8B (+24% YoY) with Google Cloud surging 82% to $24.8B, clearing analyst estimates on the top line — but shares fell roughly 5% in after-hours trading after management raised 2026 capex guidance to a projected $200B, an unprecedented scale of AI infrastructure spending that stoked investor concern about returns.
    Source: CNBC
  • AAPL Holds Near $324 — 7 Days to July 30 Earnings as Alphabet's Capex Shock Complicates Apple's $5T Push
    Apple shares are consolidating near $324 with exactly seven days until the July 30 Q3 earnings call ($1.88 EPS consensus, ~$109B revenue), but Alphabet's decline after a strong beat raises the bar for clarity — investors will now scrutinize Apple's AI capital spending commitments closely, and the $5T market-cap milestone requires a roughly 5% post-earnings move from current levels.
    Source: TheStreet
  • US-Iran Tensions Keep Oil Near $85-91; Markets Navigate Geopolitical Risk Ahead of Apple's July 30 Print
    Crude oil (Brent) has been trading in an elevated $85-91 range as US military strikes against Iran and ongoing ceasefire mediation talks keep energy markets unsettled — adding an inflation premium that could influence the Fed's September rate path and creating a headwind for VTI just as it approaches 52-week highs in what is already the most important earnings week of the summer.
    Source: Yahoo Finance

NJ Local News (Montclair)

  • Montclair Theater Festival THIS SATURDAY July 25: Free Outdoor Seussical + Shakespeare at Brookdale Park, 2-8pm
    The 2nd Annual Montclair Theater Festival returns to Brookdale Park this Saturday (July 25, 2-8pm), presented free by Vanguard Theater Company — the all-ages event features abridged professional productions of Seussical the Musical (6pm) and Shakespeare's The Tempest (3pm), plus pop-up performances from 20+ NJ theater companies, food trucks, artisan vendors, and hands-on activities for kids.
    Source: Montclair Local
  • Monmouth County Fair Through Sunday July 26 in Freehold: Rides, Live Music, and Classic Fair Food
    The 2026 Monmouth County Fair runs through Sunday July 26 at the East Freehold Showgrounds in Freehold (~45 minutes from Montclair), featuring carnival rides, competitive exhibits, live music, and local food vendors — a classic family summer fair that's one of NJ's longest-running county events.
    Source: NJ Stage
  • Paper Mill Playhouse Summer Conservatory: 'New Voices of 2026' at Montclair's Memorial Auditorium This Week
    Paper Mill Playhouse's prestigious Summer Musical Theater Conservatory presents 'New Voices of 2026: On Vacation' this week at Memorial Auditorium (1 Normal Ave, Montclair State University) — a professional-quality showcase of the next generation of musical theater talent that's ideal for theater-loving families with tweens; check papermill.org for show dates and times.
    Source: NJ Stage

Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu & Submission Grappling

  • Musumeci-Mitchell Crossover Officially Scheduled: UFC BJJ 11, September 24, Las Vegas
    After weeks as a 'homeless' challenge, the Mikey Musumeci vs. Bryce Mitchell crossover is confirmed for UFC BJJ 11 on September 24 at Meta Apex, Las Vegas; Mitchell becomes the first active UFC fighter to compete in the UFC BJJ series, facing flyweight champion Musumeci (4-0, all submissions) in a non-title featherweight bout, with Mason Fowler defending his UFC BJJ light heavyweight title vs. 2019 ADCC runner-up Nick Rodriguez in the co-main event.
    Source: MMA Mania
  • UFC BJJ 2 (July 31) Full Family Card: Tackett's Brother and Canuto's Wife Also Debut on the Free Card
    The full 10-bout UFC BJJ 2 card is set for the free July 31 YouTube stream (8pm ET): Andrew Tackett defends his welterweight title vs. Renato Canuto in the main event and Fowler vs. Garmo crowns the inaugural light heavyweight champion in the co-main — a compelling family subplot sees Andrew's brother William Tackett and Renato's wife Raquel Canuto both making their UFC BJJ debuts on the undercard.
    Source: UFC
  • UFC BJJ Series Maps to Event 11 — With 14 Cards Planned in 2026, No-Gi's Fastest-Growing League Keeps Expanding
    The announcement of UFC BJJ 11 (September 24) — featuring Musumeci-Mitchell headlining and Fowler-Rodriguez in the co-main — shows how quickly the series has scaled since its January 2026 debut; with 14 events planned for the calendar year and a growing roster of champions across weight classes, the UFC's no-gi circuit is cementing its place alongside ADCC, Polaris, and Fight to Win as a top-tier destination for elite grapplers.
    Source: FloGrappling

Global & European Soccer

  • Arsenal-Atletico Swap Talks: Viktor Gyokeres Plus €60M Cash Offered for Julian Alvarez
    Arsenal have proposed sending Swedish striker Viktor Gyokeres (valued at €65M+) plus approximately €60M cash to Atletico Madrid in exchange for Julian Alvarez — a structure that emerged after Atletico blocked a direct Alvarez sale to La Liga rivals Barcelona 'as a matter of honor'; TEAMtalk reports no agreement has been struck yet but lines of communication between the clubs remain open.
    Source: FootballTransfers
  • Atletico Pre-Season Week 2: Full Squad Expected by July 28 — Four Days to Prepare for Stockholm Aug 1
    Non-World-Cup players are training at Majadahonda this week while Spanish and Argentine World Cup finalists remain on mandatory extended rest; the full group including Grimaldo, Baena, Alvarez, G. Simeone, and Almada is expected to reassemble by July 28, giving Simeone just four training sessions before the August 1 Stockholm friendly vs. Manchester United at Strawberry Arena.
    Source: Football Espana
  • Atletico's Attacking Future in Flux: If Gyokeres Swap Closes, Salah Chase Continues — Entirely New Front Three Possible
    Atletico's summer transfer math is evolving rapidly: if the Alvarez-Gyokeres swap closes, the Swedish striker fills the void left by Sorloth's imminent Juventus departure, while the Mohamed Salah free-agent pursuit continues in parallel — Simeone could end the 2026 window with an entirely new front three compared to the La Liga title-winning season.
    Source: Goal.com

Financial Freedom & Markets

  • Alphabet Reports Q2 Tonight After Close — First Mag7 Print Sets Tone for AAPL (July 30) and SPOT (Aug 4)
    Alphabet releases its Q2 2026 results after tonight's closing bell (consensus: $2.89 EPS, $116.84B revenue, Google Cloud ~63% YoY growth); options markets are pricing a 5.4% swing in GOOGL, and as the first Magnificent Seven company to report this earnings cycle, the result will directly shape market sentiment heading into Apple's July 30 and Spotify's August 4 reports — the two most consequential remaining prints for VTI and tech broadly.
    Source: Yahoo Finance
  • AAPL 8 Days to July 30 Earnings — Tim Cook's Final Call as CEO Before John Ternus Succession; $5T Cap in Sight
    With VTI dipping to 369.45 and Apple shares consolidating near $325-330, the July 30 Q3 earnings call is shaping up as a milestone: analysts project $1.88 EPS on ~$109B revenue, but the bigger story is that July 30 will mark Tim Cook's final earnings call as CEO — hardware executive John Ternus takes over as Apple's next chief, and a strong beat could push AAPL's market cap past $5 trillion for the first time.
    Source: 247 Wall St.
  • SPOT Down 38% From ATH but Bank of America Reiterates 40% Upside — Audiobooks+ Hits $100M ARR Milestone in July
    Spotify shares (near $492, down 38% from their June 2025 peak) face a 13-day countdown to August 4 earnings, but Bank of America is reiterating a Buy thesis citing an 'impressive compelling product roadmap'; a positive pre-earnings development: Audiobooks+ is expected to confirm $100M in annualized recurring revenue this month — less than a year after launch and well ahead of schedule — a strong leading indicator for the Q2 earnings call.
    Source: Benzinga

NJ Local News (Montclair)

  • Pig & Butter Opening July 31 in Montclair: Brunch-All-Day and Unionville Vineyards Wine at 401 Orange Road
    Montclair's newest restaurant, Pig & Butter, brings a dual concept to 401 Orange Road: a full-service brunch, dinner, and cocktail spot featuring wines from Unionville Vineyards alongside a separate coffeehouse and eatery; a ribbon-cutting ceremony is set for July 31 at 10am — the same day MM by Morimoto opens on Glenridge Ave, making July 31 the biggest day for Montclair dining in recent memory.
    Source: Montclair Local
  • The Saint Clair Launches Culinary Masters Class Series Tomorrow — 'Summer Seafood Secrets,' July 23, 6:30pm
    The Saint Clair restaurant in Montclair kicks off its new culinary Masters Class series tomorrow (Thursday, July 23) at 6:30pm with 'Summer Seafood Secrets' — an intimate, hands-on cooking evening for seafood enthusiasts; the series is planned to run regularly through the fall, and seats are limited so book directly with the restaurant.
    Source: Montclair Local
  • Montclair History Center Kids' Summer Workshops Start July 27 — Hands-On Morning Programs at 9am Through August
    The Montclair History Center (108 Orange Road) launches its next round of hands-on kids' summer workshops on Monday July 27 and Tuesday July 28 at 9am — part of an ongoing summer series with activities suitable for all ages including tweens, continuing through August; free or low-cost, details at montclairnjusa.org.
    Source: Montclair History Center

Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu & Submission Grappling

  • PSS 7 Final Preview: Jacob Rodriguez vs. Vagner Rocha in Miami This Thursday — ADCC Stakes High for Both
    Jacob Rodriguez steps back onto the mat Thursday (July 24) at Karate Combat's Pit Submission Series 7 in Miami for his return from a 17-month hiatus, facing veteran Vagner Rocha in a bout laden with family history — Rodriguez submitted Vagner's son Achilles by RNC at ADCC 2024 — with significant ADCC Krakow seeding implications for both men eight weeks before the September 12-13 world championship.
    Source: BJJ Eastern Europe
  • ADCC 66kg, 77kg and 88kg Slots Open After Three Champs Withdraw — Krakow Bracket Continues to Take Shape
    With Diogo Reis (66kg), Mica Galvao (77kg), and Giancarlo Bodoni (88kg) officially off the September 12-13 ADCC World Championship roster, the promotion is working to finalize replacement invitees for each vacated seed — potentially reshuffling all three weight classes and opening title-shot opportunities for unseeded alternates who impressed at the 2026 regional trial circuit.
    Source: MMA Mania
  • F2W 322 Fresno This Saturday July 26 — Submission Grappling Circuit Rolls On With ADCC Krakow Eight Weeks Out
    Fight to Win 322 heads to Fresno on Saturday July 26 with a full no-gi card, keeping the weekly pre-ADCC grappling calendar intact as the circuit enters its final stretch before the September 12-13 World Championship; the promotion also confirmed its first-ever Brazil event is in the works, expanding its footprint ahead of what is shaping up to be grappling's biggest commercial year.
    Source: FloGrappling

Global & European Soccer

  • Atletico Madrid Pre-Season Begins Today — World Cup Players on Extended Rest, Stockholm Friendly August 1 the Target Date
    Atletico Madrid's 2026-27 pre-season training kicked off today (July 21) with a reduced group, as Spanish champions Baena, Grimaldo, Pubill, and Llorente plus Argentine finalists Alvarez, Almada, G. Simeone, and Molina remain on mandatory post-World-Cup rest; the full squad is expected to assemble by August 1 ahead of the Stockholm pre-season friendly against Manchester United at Strawberry Arena.
    Source: Atletico Madrid Official
  • Besiktas Enter Salah Race With First Formal Offer as Atletico Madrid Work on Salary Package
    Turkish giants Besiktas have made the first formal offer for free-agent Mohamed Salah, entering a race that now includes Atletico Madrid, Saudi Pro League clubs, and reported interest from other European sides; Atletico are working to construct a salary package competitive enough to beat Saudi offers, believing Champions League football under Simeone is the key differentiator for the Egyptian captain.
    Source: TNT Sports
  • Atletico 2026-27 Squad Crystallizes: Grimaldo and Hjulmand In, Sorloth to Juventus, Salah the Last Missing Piece
    As pre-season begins, Atletico Madrid's 2026-27 shape is coming into focus: confirmed new arrivals Alejandro Grimaldo (LB, 22M euros) and Morten Hjulmand (DM, 40M euros) fill two key positions; Alexander Sorloth's move to Juventus is near with clubs around 5M euros apart on a ~35M euro fee; and Julian Alvarez stays after the 150M euro Real Madrid rejection — leaving Mohamed Salah as the one remaining transfer target before La Liga kicks off in late August.
    Source: ESPN

Financial Freedom & Markets

  • Alphabet and Tesla Headline Massive Earnings Week — S&P 500 Blended Growth 24.7%; AAPL Opens at $331.98
    The busiest week of Q2 2026 earnings season opens with Alphabet (GOOGL) reporting Wednesday after close — analysts project $2.87 EPS on $116.8-120.2B revenue with Google Cloud up 63% YoY — and Tesla Thursday; S&P 500 blended earnings growth stands at 24.7% with 87% of early reporters beating estimates, lifting VTI near its 52-week high as AAPL opens at $331.98 today, nine days from its own July 30 earnings report.
    Source: Forbes
  • NJ 30-Year Refinance Rate Jumps to 7.02% — Up From 6.65% Last Week as Bond Markets Price Fewer Fed Cuts
    New Jersey's average 30-year fixed mortgage refinance rate has risen to 7.02% (15-year: 6.04%), reversing last week's 6.65% level as bond markets price fewer near-term Fed rate cuts; NJ homeowners eyeing a refinance should monitor closely — a softer-than-expected Alphabet or Apple earnings print this week or next could pull rates back, while waiting risks further increases if economic data stays hot.
    Source: Wirly
  • SPOT: 14 Days to August 4 Earnings — Jefferies Projects Steady Quarter; AI Remixing Timeline Is the Key Catalyst
    With Spotify's Q2 report 14 days away (August 4, before market open), Jefferies projects a steady print — 33.1% gross margin and 17M net new MAUs — but views the quarter as unlikely to be 'narrative-changing'; the stock's path to its $678 analyst consensus price target (37% upside from ~$494) depends almost entirely on management providing a concrete rollout timeline for the AI remixing feature at the earnings call.
    Source: Yahoo Finance

NJ Local News (Montclair)

  • Colson Whitehead at Montclair State TOMORROW (July 22) — Two-Time Pulitzer Winner Presents Final Harlem Trilogy Novel
    Two-time Pulitzer Prize winner Colson Whitehead appears at MSU's Memorial Auditorium (1 Normal Ave, Montclair) tomorrow July 22 at 7pm to discuss 'Cool Machine,' the conclusion to his Harlem Trilogy, in conversation with book critic Kate Tuttle; tickets are $45.99 and include a signed copy of the novel, with a post-show signing to follow — book now at tickettailor.com.
    Source: Montclair Local
  • Sourland Mountain Festival This Saturday July 25 in Ringoes — Family Scavenger Hunt, Live Music, Food at Unionville Vineyards
    The 2026 Sourland Mountain Festival returns Saturday July 25 (3pm-dusk) at Unionville Vineyards, 9 Rocktown Road, East Amwell Township (~40 min from Montclair), with live music from regional bands, a family scavenger hunt, and local food and craft beer; only 1,000 tickets available, advance purchase recommended at sourlandmountainfest.com.
    Source: Eventbrite
  • Montclair Jazz Soundcheck Monday July 28: Joel Ross' Good Vibes Honors Chicago at Lackawanna Plaza — Free, 6-10pm
    The Montclair Jazz Festival's free weekly Soundcheck Series continues Monday July 28 with Grammy-nominated vibraphonist Joel Ross and his quartet Good Vibes performing at Lackawanna Station (1 Lackawanna Plaza), 6-10pm — part of the festival's 2026 'American Jazz Cities' theme honoring Chicago; free and open to all, no registration required.
    Source: VisitNJ

Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu & Submission Grappling

    ADCC has confirmed the removal of three sitting division champions from its Krakow 2026 roster: Diogo Reis (66kg), Mica Galvao (77kg), and Giancarlo Bodoni (88kg), alongside West Coast Trials winner Elder Cruz — reshuffling three weight classes and opening significant bracket opportunities for unseeded grapplers eight weeks before the September 12–13 event.

    FloGrappling's July 20 weekly bulletin highlights the sport's explosive 2026 growth: IBJJF No-Gi Worlds registration has opened for a late-year date; the UFC BJJ series — which launched in January with 14 events planned for 2026 — is already scheduling event 8; and Fight to Win is staging its first-ever Brazilian show, signaling grappling's global commercial reach.

    Atlético CEO Miguel Ángel Gil Marín formally lodged a FIFA and RFEF complaint accusing Barcelona of illegally approaching Julián Álvarez; separately, Atlético also rejected a €150M bid from Real Madrid for the striker, publicly mocking both clubs, even as Barcelona prepares a revised offer of up to €135–150M.

    Lee Kang-in has agreed personal terms with Atlético Madrid on a contract through 2031 for a fee of approximately €35M, with his PSG exit now confirmed; if completed, he would become the first Asian player ever to represent Atlético.

    With No-Gi Brasileiros wrapped up and the Polaris 33 bracket now released, the summer grappling schedule shifts to the IBJJF American Nationals as athletes build final ADCC Worlds preparation ahead of the Krakow event in September.

    Atlético turned down Barcelona's initial €100M bid for Julián Álvarez and are holding firm at €150M, but direct club-to-club meetings are now confirmed; Atlético privately concede the departure is near-inevitable after Simeone reportedly lost patience following the player's public transfer request.

    Paraguay pulled off a massive Round of 32 upset, beating Germany 4–3 on penalties after a 1–1 draw, while Morocco similarly shocked the Netherlands 3–2 in a shootout; France plays Sweden tonight (June 30) at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford at 5pm ET.

    Leon Goretzka's Bayern Munich contract expired June 30, making him a free agent with Atlético Madrid among interested clubs; however, his ~€15M/year salary demands are beyond what Atlético can accommodate, with Sporting's Morten Hjulmand remaining the club's top midfield target.

    Apple ended the quarter near $282 with a Buy consensus (avg. target $315); Counterpoint Research forecasts iPhone's global market share rising to 25% and Mac to 12% by year-end, suggesting demand remains resilient despite recent device price hikes driven by memory shortages.
    Source: GuruFocus

    Spotify shares remain deeply in the red for 2026, but Q2 guidance targets 778M monthly active users and €4.8B in revenue (+15% y/y) with gross margin near 33.1%; with 34+ analysts maintaining buy ratings and earnings due July 29 before market open, the report is the next major inflection point.

Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu & Submission Grappling

  • King Charles III Visits Roger Gracie Academy, Receives BJJ White Belt
    King Charles III toured Roger Gracie Academy's London headquarters and was awarded a white belt by Roger Gracie himself, in a visit spotlighting Reorg, a military and emergency-responder charity that uses jiu-jitsu in veterans' recovery; the King also presented a black belt to a Reorg trustee who credits the sport with helping him through cancer treatment.

    Just days after announcing B-Team's revival, Craig Jones gave a blunt interview admitting to long-term steroid use — including injecting before EBI in Tijuana — and said he considers it cheating but stays open about it because 'the next generation is gonna take it anyway.'
    Source: BJJ Eastern Europe

    Britain's Owen Jones avenged a three-year-old loss to Fabricio 'Hokage' Andrey, edging him on the scorecards after a tense leg-lock battle to win the night's lone grappling bout and snap Andrey's three-fight win streak in ONE Championship.
    Source: ONE Championship
  • ADCC 2026 Invite List Pulled From Website Amid Transparency Backlash
    With ADCC Worlds set for September in Krakow, organizers quietly removed their official invite and qualification list from the website without explanation, leaving fans to piece together the lineup from athlete announcements and fueling debate over contested invites like Josh Saunders' return.
    Source: BJJ Eastern Europe

Global & European Soccer

  • Álex Baena's Strike Sends Spain Top of Group, Knocks Out Uruguay
    Atlético midfielder Álex Baena scored the only goal in the 42nd minute as Spain beat Uruguay 1-0 in Guadalajara, topping Group H and eliminating Uruguay from the World Cup while Cape Verde also advanced to the Round of 32.
    Source: ESPN
  • Atlético Set to Sign Stuttgart Midfielder Enzo Millot by Triggering €23M Release Clause
    Atlético have agreed personal terms with Stuttgart's Enzo Millot and plan to trigger his €23 million release clause, with Simeone targeting the playmaker — who scored 12 goals last season — as the club's eighth summer signing.

    Ousmane Dembélé scored three first-half goals as France routed Norway 4-1 at the World Cup; Norway rested Atlético's Alexander Sørloth and Erling Haaland but still advanced to the Round of 32 as Group I runner-up.

    Source: Simply Wall St

    PSE&G has automatically enrolled residential customers in a new Time-of-Use plan charging about $0.31/kWh during weekday 4-9pm peak hours versus roughly $0.09/kWh off-peak, with a 12-month savings guarantee for households that shift laundry and EV charging to nights and weekends.

Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu & Submission Grappling

    Ben Eddy, who took bronze at -70kg with four submission wins, was slammed by blue belt Jakori Savage during overtime of the absolute division at the ADCC Dallas-Fort Worth Open, drawing a disqualification; Eddy said he escaped without serious injury.

    UFC lightweight champion Islam Makhachev says he has received offers to compete in standalone grappling and wrestling super-fights but is declining them, citing camp demands and injury risk outside his MMA schedule.

    Tom Pestock, known to wrestling fans as Baron Corbin, added another medal to his growing competitive BJJ resume with a gold-medal finish at a Jiu-Jitsu World League tournament.

    Atlético confirmed Alejandro Grimaldo as a new player on a deal through 2029 (plus an optional fourth year) for a fixed €15M fee plus variables, with the left-back saying he's 'always liked Atlético' ahead of his move to the Metropolitano.

    The United States lost 3-2 to Turkey at SoFi Stadium on a last-gasp Kaan Ayhan goal in a dead-rubber match, having already clinched first place in Group D and a Round of 32 date with Bosnia and Herzegovina.

    Fresh off a brace against Senegal, Atlético striker Alexander Sørloth lines up with Norway against France on June 26 in Foxborough with first place in Group I on the line ahead of the World Cup Round of 32.

    Asian and U.S. tech stocks fell to a two-week low after a report said OpenAI may push its IPO into 2027, sending SoftBank shares down as much as 13% and reviving fears about AI-spending payoffs even as fresh data showed the U.S. economy growing faster than estimated.

    Facing a $255 million budget deficit, Jersey City's mayor yanked a proposed 20% property tax increase from the June 24 council agenda after public outcry; a new vote is set for July 1, with the average $11,000 tax bill potentially rising nearly $2,000 if it proceeds.

    Ruotolo pulled out of his scheduled ONE Lightweight Submission Grappling World Title defense against Fabricio Andrey after sustaining an injury in his recent MMA win; Andrey has instead been rebooked against newcomer Owen Jones at ONE Fight Night 44 in Bangkok.

    Roberto Frias scored one of the trials' biggest upsets by beating favorite Lucas Kanard to win the -88kg title, while Kaya Rudolph, Bekzat Kapashov, and women's qualifiers Nadia Frankland and Matilda Reid also punched their tickets to ADCC Worlds in Krakow.

    BJJ legend Beatriz "Bia" Mesquita stayed undefeated in the UFC, submitting Melissa Mullins with a first-round armbar at UFC Vegas 119 after surviving an early scare, and immediately called out Ailin Perez for a future matchup.

    Atlético Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen have closed a club-to-club deal for left-back Alejandro Grimaldo in the €20-25M range, with the player signing through 2029 plus an option — multiple outlets now call it done pending his medical and official presentation once Spain's World Cup run ends.

    Atlético CEO Miguel Ángel Gil Marín announced the club will lodge a complaint with FIFA accusing Barcelona of negotiating with Julián Álvarez — under contract until 2030 — during the protected period, escalating the saga from rhetoric into formal regulatory action.

item.content:encoded:
Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu & Submission Grappling

  • Tainan Dalpra Wins Fourth IBJJF World Title With All-Submission Run in Under Six Minutes Total
    At the 2026 IBJJF World Championship in Long Beach, AOJ's Tainan Dalpra captured his fourth middleweight world title by submitting all four opponents in just six minutes of total mat time — one of the most dominant Worlds performances in the sport's history. Dalpra and Gabi Pessanha were the only two athletes to complete the full IBJJF Grand Slam in 2026, and both are now eyeing ADCC 2026 in Poland this September where they could pursue a rare Super Grand Slam. Dalpra also became the first male athlete to earn two IBJJF Grand Slam titles in a single season.
    Source: IBJJF

Global & European Soccer

  • Atlético Madrid on Verge of Signing Bayer Leverkusen's Grimaldo as Left-Back Replacement
    Atlético Madrid are reportedly close to finalizing a deal for Spanish left-back Alejandro Grimaldo from Bayer Leverkusen, with Leverkusen executives in Madrid to accelerate talks and a deal potentially wrapping up on June 24. Grimaldo, 30, had been pushing for a return to La Liga this summer with his Leverkusen contract expiring in 2027, and Atlético turned to him after missing out on Chelsea's Marc Cucurella to Real Madrid. The move would give Simeone a proven Bundesliga attacking full-back as the club simultaneously manages the ongoing Julián Álvarez transfer saga.
    Source: Tribuna.com

Financial Freedom & Markets

  • Markets Attempt Rebound Wednesday After Two-Day Tech Rout; Micron Earnings Loom as Key AI Test
    After the S&P 500 fell 1.44% and the Nasdaq dropped 2.21% on Tuesday — led by a collapse in chip stocks including Micron (-13%), AMD (-5.8%), and Qualcomm (-8%) — futures pointed higher Wednesday morning as traders look to bargain-hunt. All eyes are on Micron's after-bell earnings report, where analysts expect roughly $35 billion in sales, as a critical read on AI infrastructure demand. Adding to macro uncertainty, BofA and Deutsche Bank now both forecast the Fed will raise rates three times in 2026 under Chair Kevin Warsh, with hikes projected in September, October, and December.
    Source: 24/7 Wall St.
  • NJ Mortgage Rates Hold in Mid-to-High 6% Range as Home Prices and Property Taxes Stay Elevated
    New Jersey's 30-year fixed mortgage rate sits between approximately 6.69% and 6.88% as of late June 2026, slightly above the national average, with monthly payments on a median-priced NJ home (~$563,000 with 20% down) running close to $3,000 before taxes. NJ also holds the nation's highest effective property tax rate at 2.49%, translating to roughly $830/month in escrow on a $400K home. With BofA forecasting potential Fed rate hikes later this year, would-be refinancers and buyers should act with caution, though more than 52% of NJ homeowners are currently equity-rich.
    Source: Bankrate

NJ Local News (Montclair)

  • Montclair Flea Returns This Weekend at Lackawanna Plaza — Family-Friendly Vendors, Food, and Vintage Finds
    The Montclair Flea is back at 1 Lackawanna Plaza on Saturday June 27 (11am–5pm) and Sunday June 28 (11am–5pm), featuring curated vendors with art, vintage items, food, and drinks — described as a fun, rain-or-shine outing for the whole family. It's a great low-key option for a 12-year-old who enjoys browsing unique finds, grabbing a bite, or soaking up the outdoor scene in downtown Montclair. The event runs through the summer and holiday season as well.
    Source: Lackawanna Station
  • Montclair Pride Festival Moved to August 1 — Free All-Day Event with Live Music, Drag, Food Trucks, and Family Zone
    Out Montclair has officially rescheduled the 2026 Montclair Pride Festival from June 13 to Saturday, August 1, citing financial and operational requirements needed to safely produce the event and keep it free and accessible. The downtown Montclair festival will feature live music, drag performances, food trucks, a family zone, bar areas, and an evening street-dance party. Families with kids can enjoy the family zone, and the rescheduled date gives more time to plan a summer outing.
    Source: The Montclair Girl
